Special Branch, XXXX 8.12.37
REPORT
Date Dec. 8, 1937.7

Subject Objectionable article appearing in the "Chung Kuo Er Tung"

Made by and Forwarded by C.D.I. Ross.

Acting on instructions of D. C. (Special Branch)
on the attached translation of an article entitled "The Son
of Widow Ma" from the "Chung Kuo Er Tung" (中國兒童 "Chinese
Children"), a ten-day periodical, of December 5, Mr. Wong
Zung-loo (王人路), editor of the periodical in question,
was interviewed at Police Headquarters at 11.30 a.m.
December 8, when he was warned by the P. A. to D. C. (Special
Branch) to refrain from publishing articles of this nature,
or else his publication should be removed from the
International Settlement.

In reply, Mr. Wong promised to exercise greater
care in future.

C. D. I.
D. C. (Special Branch).

December 7, 1937.
Afternoon Translation.

Chung Kuo Er Tung (中國兒童), a ten-day periodical, dated
December 5, :-

THE SON OF WIDOW MA

On a certain small street in the factory zone
in the Eastern District stands a small cigarette shop
bearing the signboard "The Yung Yui Ziang Shop" (永裕祥).
Its customers are mostly workers. The keeper of the shop
is a man named Ma (馬); his wife and a young son named
Siao New (小牛) are the assistants.
One day, a year later, a notice was posted
up before the shop stating that business has been
suspended because of a funeral service.
The widow Ma understood that her husband had
lost his life at the hands of ronins who possessed certain
influence in Hongkew. The following narration shows
how her husband met his death :-
One evening the shop-keeper Ma drank some wine
and being in high spirits he abused certain traitors who
had been going everywhere acting as agents for the "Lou
Tou Eye Medicine" (老篤眼藥) and another remedy known
as "Stomach Survival" (胃活). He also badly abused
the XX ronins and women. That evening he was assaulted
when walking home alone, and was seriously injured.
As he lay at the point of death, he shouted : "Well, you
may assault me, you may assault me! If I die, I still
have a son! The people of China do not fear death!"
Ma's son had now learned by heart this
sentence: "Overthrow XX people".
When questioned by anybody how his father had
died, the boy would reply at once that his father was
fatally assaulted by XX people.
Q:- Do you want to avenge the death of your father?
A:- Certainly.
Q:- In what way can you avenge the death of your father?
A:- I will do my best to read and write.
Q:- What's the use of this?
A:- So that I may write slogans to inform the public
which people are bad so that the general public
might overthrow them.
All this took place three years ago. At
present, the Eastern District has been razed by fire and
it has become a place for lawless elements. Large
numbers of persons have suffered the same fate as Siao
New's father. The widow Ma and her son have become
refugees and their whereabouts are unknown.

（印：213 -7 DEC 1937 SPECIAL MUNICIPAL POLICE）

1937年12月7日。
下午译文。

《中國兒童》，一份旬刊，日期为12月5日，内容如下：-

马寡妇的儿子

在东区工厂区的一条小街上，有一家挂着“永裕祥”招牌的小烟纸店。其顾客多为工人。店主姓马；他的妻子和一个名叫小牛的儿子是帮手。
一年后的一天，店前贴出一张告示，称因办理丧事暂停营业。
马寡妇得知，她的丈夫是被在虹口具有一定势力的浪人所害。以下叙述说明了她丈夫遇害的经过：-
一天晚上，店主马某喝了一些酒，兴致高涨，便辱骂某些四处充当“老篤眼藥”和另一种名为“胃活”的药品代理人的汉奸。他还恶毒地辱骂了XX浪人和妇女。当晚，他在独自回家途中遭到袭击，身受重伤。
在他弥留之际，他喊道：“好吧，你们可以打我，你们可以打我！如果我死了，我还有一个儿子！中国人民不怕死！”
马的儿子现在已经背熟了这句话：“推翻XX人”。
当任何人问起他父亲是如何去世时，男孩会立即回答说他父亲是被XX人殴打致死的。
问：你想为你父亲的死报仇吗？
答：当然。
问：你如何为你父亲的死报仇？
答：我会尽力读书写字。
问：这有什么用？
答：这样我就可以写标语告知公众哪些人是坏人，以便大众推翻他们。
这一切发生在三年前。目前，东区已被战火夷为平地，已成为不法之徒聚集之地。许多人遭遇了与小牛父亲相同的命运。马寡妇和她的儿子已成为难民，下落不明。

（印：213 -1937年12月7日 特别市警察）

REPORT
Date October 3, 1937

Subject The Chinese Children's National Salvation Association - publication
entitled "The Chinese Children."
Made by C.D.I. Sih Tse-liang Forwarded by C. Crawford. D.D.

With reference to the remarks of D. C. (Crime & Special
Branches), the No. 2 issue of "The Chinese Children", mentioned
in the attached report of October 1, contains the following
pictures allegedly drawn by children:-

(1) A Chinese soldier carrying a national flag bearing the
slogan, "Long Live the Republic of China!"

(2) Chinese ladies sewing vests for the use of soldiers.

(3) Chinese soldiers on guard with the remarks, "The enemy
will advance no further."

(4) A soldier attacking his enemy with the remarks, "Hail.
Where have you fled to?"

(5) An armed civilian pointing his bayonet towards a soldier
in uniform with the remarks, "Do you see it?"

(6) A gun position with the words "Aiming at the enemy."

(7) A boy carrying a banner bearing the characters "Children's
National Salvation Association." Remarks: "Rise up,
little friends throughout China!"

(8) A soldier blowing a bugle with the remarks, "Rush foward."

(9) A soldier bayonetting his enemy, marked "Look here."

(10) A soldier, marked "Kill and Kill, the enemy is afraid to
come again."

(11) A soldier defeating his enemy, marked "We shall never
forgive you!"

(12) A defeated soldier (appears to be a Japanese), marked,
"Where have you to retreat?"

(13) A Chinese soldier in advance position, marked, "Rise up
and rush forward amidst enemy gunfire!"

(14) A soldier advancing through burning fire, marked, "Our
spirit is as brilliant as the burning fire."

（印：4 OCT. 1937）
（批：S.1. / K.V. / D.R. / 4/10）
（批：C / 8/10）

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
File No. S. B. D 270
S. 1. Special Branch
REPORT
Date October 1, 1937

Subject (in full) The Chinese Childrens National Salvation Association -
broadcast programme for September 28, 29, and 30, 1937.

Made by D. I. Pan Lieh-pih Forwarded by C. Gafana 2.1.

The programme of broadcasting, sponsored by the Chinese
Children's National Salvation Association for the three days
commencing September 28, and which was to take place over
a broadcasting set installed in the Shanghai Amusement Circles'
National Salvation Association, 5 Boo Liu Faung, Avenue
Edward VII, was cancelled following the refusal of the manage-
ment of the Grand Hotel, Yu Ya Ching Road, who own the set
to permit the broadcasting because of previous warnings by
the Police.

Attached to this report is a copy of the "Chinese Children"
Issue No. 2, which is a special one, devoted to the publication
of cartoons bearing on the national salvation movement and
which are allegedly drawn by the children.

（印：RECEIVED COMMISSIONER 4 OCT. 1937 H.）
Pan Lien-pih
D. I.

D. C. (Crime & Special Branches). S.I.

Date September 28, 1937.

Subject The Chinese Childrens National Salvation Association - broadcast
programme for September 28, 29, and 30, 1937.
Made by D.I. Fan Lieh-pih    Forwarded by C. Gauda. D.J.

（印：RECEIVED 30 SEPT. 1937 SHANGHAI）

The Chinese Children's National Salvation Association,
which is situated in the upper floor of the Dah Chung
(大中) Restaurant, 706 Avenue Edward VII. was organized
at the beginning of September, 1937, by Mr. Won, Yao (温尧),
ex-proof-reader of the Sin Yan Pao Newspaper Office, 274
Hankow Road, and Mr. Won: Zung Loo (王人路), editor of the
Childrens Section of the Sin Yan Evening News, under the
auspices of Mr. Chu Hsueh Fan, Chairman of the General
Labour Union. The object of the association is to raise
funds for the relief of war refugees and provide comforts
for Chinese soldiers. The membership consists at present
of only ten children, including a few child actors belonging
to the local motion picture companies.

（批：Ag. C.P. Information）
（印：30 SEP. 1937 (C)）

It is the intention of the Chinese Childrens National
Salvation Association to broadcast songs and plays over the
radio station belonging to the Shanghai Amusement Circles
National Salvation Association, No. 5 Boo Liu Faung (步留坊),
Avenue Edward VII. between 5 p.m. and 5.40 p.m..and 6 p.m.
and 6.40 p.m. on September 28, 29, and 30, 1937, in order
to raise funds to provide relief for war refugees and to
purchase vests for Chinese soldiers.

The programme for September 28 is as follows:-
From 5 p.m. to 5.40 p.m., September 28
Speeches by children actors on national crisis.
Singing of songs: "A Stray Goat (迷途的羔羊)",
"Joining the Army (從軍去)", and "Consolation Song
(慰勞歌)", as well as dance music.
From 6 p.m. to 6.40 p.m., September 28.
Broadcasting of a play entitled "Amidst Gunfire," 炮火中

（批：Further Inf.）
（批：S.I. as indicated DR i/10）

C.D.J. Sih
C i/10

《大公报》及其他本地报纸：1937年9月25日（下午）
儿童界全国抗亡协会今日举行游艺会
儿童界全国抗亡协会今日将为各界人士举行游艺会。游艺会将展出救国图画及漫画。参加游艺会的人士每人将获赠一份《中國兒童》。

Sin Wan Pao publishes the following advertisement: 28937/241
CHILDREN TO BROADCAST PATRIOTIC PLAY THIS EVENING
Between 6 and 6.40 p.m. September 28, the
Children's National Extinction Aversion Association will
broadcast a dramatic play entitled "Amidst the Gunfire"
(炮火中) through the temporary radio station of the
Entertainers' National Extinction Aversion Association
(K.C.1080). The play referred to depicts a scene
of Paoshan Road on August 13.

《新闻报》刊登如下广告：28937/241
儿童今晚广播爱国剧
9月28日晚6时至6时40分，儿童全国抗亡协会将通过艺人全国抗亡协会（K.C.1080）的临时广播电台广播名为《炮火中》的话剧。该剧描绘了8月13日宝山路的场景。
